screenLevelIssues.explanation: The code applies 64px padding (`spacing.huge`) inside the main content. Since the parent `Screen` component typically handles Safe Area Insets (adding ~34px on iOS), the total visual space from the bottom bezel will be ~98px. Figma designs usually measure padding from the device edge, inclusive of the home indicator area.
screenLevelIssues.fixedCode: paddingBottom: spacing.huge, // Ensure parent Screen has safeAreaEdges={['top']} or subtract insets

screenLevelIssues.explanation: Using a fixed height `sv(613)` for the main container combined with `justifyContent: 'space-between'` forces a rigid vertical rhythm. On devices with different aspect ratios (e.g., taller phones), this may cause the content to float higher than intended or clip if the screen is shorter than the scaled value.
screenLevelIssues.currentCode: height: sv(613), // Figma Container height (NOT 852 root screen height)
screenLevelIssues.fixedCode: minHeight: sv(613), // Use minHeight to allow expansion

layoutIssues.explanation: The heading text uses manual newlines (`\n`) to force line breaks. If the device width is narrower than the design (297px) or user font scaling is enabled, this can cause awkward double-wrapping (e.g., 'Make' on one line, 'your' on next, 'rent' on next).
layoutIssues.currentCode:
<Text style={styles.headingGray}>
                Make{'\n'}your rent{'\n'}
                <Text style={styles.headingAccent}>work for you→</Text>
              </Text>
layoutIssues.fixedCode:
<Text style={styles.headingGray}>
                Make your rent <Text style={styles.headingAccent}>work for you→</Text>
              </Text>
